note:
Independent final source rejudgment of RFC2918-4-3, 2026-11-19. Main's final configured-refresh healthy/broken receipts and canonical discrimination record were independently read before this verdict. RFC 2918 was read in full, including Section 4: Otherwise the speaker shall re-advertise to that peer the Adj-RIB-Out of the carried AFI/SAFI, based on its outbound route filtering policy. Preserve enforced and all eight existing bindings; no requirement, tag, polarity, capability or whole-RFC support scope is changed.

The four tagged RIB roots retain their existing legacy observation scope. ConfigStaticRetainedForRefresh records an actual structured config-static SENT UPDATE on the attached original owner/session, drives an IPv4 refresh, parses the production update commands and requires exactly 198.51.100.0/24 with byte-identical original attributes. Config-static remains excluded from peer-up replay before and after replay feedback, remains in refresh inventory, and a genuinely local plugin replacement becomes peer-up eligible. RefreshDoesNotSendToDownPeer seeds useful Adj-RIB-Out, installs separate failure hooks for route and marker calls, and requires neither. InternalState drives the actual event handler, parses exactly the two requested IPv4 routes with no IPv6 leakage or withdrawals, requires replay metadata on every command and both exact markers, and preserves the peer and inventory. PeerNotUp has the narrower historical body: it checks that the peer remains down after the request, without independently observing route/marker absence. Its comment is not promoted into an additional negative witness; the sibling with both refusal hooks supplies that proof.

The two Reactor roots retain their three bindings. CurrentExportPolicy uses a real compiled library policy and answer transport at the Session export gate: accept requires one policy call and grown recording bytes; flipping only the answer to reject requires a second call with exactly unchanged bytes. This proves current policy reevaluation and output/no-new-output, without independently decoding exact useful NLRI/attributes. ReplayFeedback runs both immediate and initial-sync-queued writes and requires the replay sent-event flag true before a later ordinary send's false flag. These remain actual Session writer metadata observations, not inferred origin authority.

The unchanged refresh-config-static.ci is the useful daemon witness: an explicit configured IPv4 update with the original next hop and attributes, complete attached receive-update/state/refresh and send-update/refresh grants, exact initial UPDATE and EOR, then an actual subtype-zero refresh and exact BoRR, byte-identical configured UPDATE and EoRR on the original socket. Unlike the legacy RIB hooks, that daemon now exercises the ordinary selected worker and its configured-output phase. The latest daemon after both LocalOrigin and zero-epoch defenses is job-advertiser-configured-refresh-final-wire-6acef1f4.log: the exact original refresh-config-static test is PASS 1.4s at line 7 with overall pass at 8. Main retained the current BGP implementation and original test, pinning only unrelated moving IKE compiler inputs for that build. The previously completed paired receipt is job-advertiser-configured-refresh-final-proof-9809bf24.log: healthy named refresh-config-static PASS 2.9s at line 8; intended broken named test TIME 20.0s at line 23 and failure header 29; actual handleSentStructured body-panic at line 110; native RFC2918-4-3 daemon record at 147 and break at 149. The broken peer transcript still contains the exact initial configured UPDATE and EOR at lines 45-46 and the actual refresh request, but no subsequent BoRR, replay UPDATE or EoRR. This is whole-producer dependency through actual SENT handling, not a quiet selective route-omission mutant, independent marker-order discrimination or an all-negative-leaf proof. The clean daemon's exact existing expectations provide the complete useful refresh-sequence witness. The earlier unrelated IKE compile failure in daemon-retake-9809bf24 is not counted as runtime evidence.

Current startup wiring binds both final writers before destination admission. The selected worker awaits Begin and selected-route receipts, then replayConfiguredSent, then End. The configured phase captures only keys from the current original owner's requested family whose SENT entries satisfy configuredForSession: ConfigStatic, the final writer's authenticated LocalOrigin, and the exact destination Session. The peer-wide configured marker alone is insufficient, because an interleaved learned write can inherit it. The local-origin predicate is checked at both key capture and current-entry re-read; SourceLocal comes from the final adjOutWrite.recordNLRI owner and is projected by notifyOneMessage/handleSentStructured, not inferred from an absent source address. It re-reads each key under the existing peer lock before reconstructing an owned command, verifies the live ordinary owner/session/address tuple, releases that lock before SDK I/O, and sends a destination-bound maintenance request with replay=true, original sent-owner-message and SourcePolicyEpoch deliberately zero. A configured local owner has no received-policy epoch. Independently of the observed LocalOrigin bit, the final sentOwnerCurrent/sourcePolicyCurrent checks accept an actual local owner and reject any learned owner when the request epoch is zero. The supplementary TestRFC8212SentOwnerEpochFence explicitly contrasts zero-epoch learned refusal with zero-epoch local acceptance using the actual announce path and settled wire history. Its current BGP-only race run was independently read in job-advertiser-configured-refresh-engine-guard-d5d1f341.log: whole-root PASS at 70, zero-epoch-refused PASS at 72 and local-origin-admitted PASS at 76, with package PASS at 78. That log also passes the current policy root at 19. These are related guard receipts, not additional RFC2918 tags. The new configured-worker root, including ordinary and enhanced refresh, passed after the local-origin/zero-epoch changes in job-unit-pkg-f230526a.log at 51-56, with RIB package PASS at 98; its injected sender is a worker settlement/provenance control, not an independent socket witness. The broad reactor build failure printed before the scoped engine-guard run is not counted as a runtime proof. It supplies no new selected-origin receipt and cannot promote SENT inventory into candidate authority. A replacement or withdrawal of a captured key is not resurrected from an old snapshot. On a settled error the key remains pending and is re-read for retry; an unsettled cancellation stays latched and cannot silently become a fresh attempt or End. The bounded pending set belongs only to this active refresh.

The engine's existing bound maintenance path validates original destination owner/session, waits for that destination's earlier FIFO work, and writes synchronously through actual flush rather than queuing for a replacement connection. The final exact SENT revision guard suppresses stale or removed receipts; current export policy may also intentionally suppress output. A clean legacy Announced result is therefore completion, not independent evidence of newly transmitted bytes. Expected replay preserves its original receipt revision, and replay feedback does not recreate purged ownership. Actual decoded daemon bytes provide the useful route proof; source and unit checks supply the owner/family/retry limits. This repair preserves legacy configured output and restoration; it does not claim startup configured-route origin arbitration or broader learned-source authority.

Historical renewed discrimination evidence remains bounded. In job-advertiser-rib-refresh-proof-renewal-58f7d364.log the config root is healthy at 2 and records a collector body-panic failure at 33; the strong down-peer root is healthy at 66 and records its handler body-panic failure at 91; InternalState is healthy at 118 and records sendRoutes body-panic failure at 149. In job-advertiser-legacy-refresh-and-receive-framing-proof-ae214313.log the policy clean runs at 173/269 and records at 222/318 fail on the first accepting replay, before the rejecting leaf; replay feedback is clean at 366 and records at 405 after a first-replay sendUpdateCounted panic, before its later ordinary/queued controls. Those breaks prove whole-producer dependency, not selective rejection, origin corruption or metadata discrimination. Earlier initial-sync/filter-chain judgments remain historical provenance, with their existing assertions preserved. No forwarding-plane installation, foreign acceptance or broader selected authority is inferred.
